text:
incident-bot: ALERT: GPU pool 'east-gpu-prod' queued request depth has spiked > 95% (queue length 42k). Autoscaler failing to add nodes. Paging oncall. Link: https://grafana.redwood-infra/r/d/queue/queue-overview

alex: getting paged, looking now. seeing steady increase in pending tokens and 503s from host proxies.

maria: oncall here. which customers hit? 

nina: c-svc-1 and c-svc-3 reporting client 429s + user-facing latency. CS on call confirms impact for ~4 customers (high usage).

chris: metrics: throughput down ~35% last 12m, p95 latency up from 60ms->520ms. autoscaler logs show repeated ScaleUpDenied: pool_limit_reached (max_pools=12).

sam: oh, we recently deployed a runtime config change to continuous-batching defaults 09:12 UTC. PR #1928 touched batch_window from 20ms -> 200ms and prefix-cache TTL from 10m -> 30s. suspecting that.

elena: that PR also changed KV eviction heuristics, see deploy: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/commit/ab12f9c

alex: logs (snippet):
```
2025-11-07T09:37:14Z [batcher] flush_timeout=200ms num_in_batch=1
2025-11-07T09:37:20Z [kvcache] prefix_miss_rate=0.82
2025-11-07T09:37:22Z [autoscaler] attempted_scale_up -> denied (pool_cap=12)
2025-11-07T09:37:45Z [proxy] 503 service_unavailable queued_requests=42031
```

maria: ok plan: 1) open hotfix to revert batching/prefix-ttl to previous values and rollback the deploy 2) temporarily increase pool cap and trigger manual scale 3) enable degraded fallback model variant for affected routes 4) notify customers. Assigning tasks.

chris: I'll handle pool cap bump. Running: `rctl pools set-cap east-gpu-prod --max 18` and then `rctl pools scale east-gpu-prod --replicas 6`

alex: I'm preparing rollback PR to restore batch_window=20ms and prefix_cache_ttl=10m. PR link: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/1950 (hotfix).

sam: I'll flip route fallback to smaller model (gpt-small-2) for customer-facing routes to reduce per-request tokens. patch: `routes/prod-fallback.yaml` updated, applying.

jake: posting status to customers who asked for ETA. message drafted: "We're investigating a degradation affecting inference throughput in us-east; mitigation in progress; temporary reduced throughput and elevated errors expected for ~30-60m."

sli-monitor: ALERT: Error budget burn > 15% in last 10m. Noted.

elena: autoscaler reason for denial: internal rate of scale operations hit (scale_ops_rate_limit). also hitting quota for reserved gpus for dedicated customers — need approval. I'll request emergency quota bump from cloud.

maria: timeline so far: 09:12 deploy change -> 09:28 queue growth observed -> 09:34 paging -> 09:37 confirmed prefix cache missstorm + scale denied.

alex: applying hotfix now (rolling restart of runtime service with prior config). running `kubectl apply -f runtime-hotfix-1950.yaml`

chris: pool cap updated, manual scale initiated. replicas increased: 3 -> 6. observing CPU/GPU allocations spin up.

sam: fallback route applied. traffic slicing shows ~25% now on gpt-small-2. error rate for affected customers improving slowly.

10:02 alex: hotfix applied, batch_window=20ms restored and prefix_cache_ttl=10m. taking effect; seeing cache hit rate climb.

10:07 sli-monitor: prefix_cache_hit_rate from 18% -> 72% in 5m. queue length 42k -> 3.4k. p95 latency trending down.

10:11 maria: confirm manual scale completed, pool replicas stable. autoscaler now has headroom, no further ScaleUpDenied errors.

nina: CS updated impacted customers, two asked for more details; provided ETA and remediation steps.

jake: DH: Are we comfortable keeping fallback routes for 2h and then revert? product wants 1h.

sam: keep for 2h to be safe, but monitor.

elena: cloud granted temporary quota increase for pool cap. we should still track reserved GPU usage and bill impact. I'll log cost notes in incident ticket.

maria: great. documenting actions: rollback runtime config PR#1950 merged, pool cap bumped to 18, manual scale to 6 replicas, fallback routing to gpt-small-2 for 2h.

alex: initializing post-incident checklist and brief ticket: https://issues.redwood/productivity/INC-2981. assigning to eng-runtime (owner: elena) and eng-autoscaler (owner: chris).

chris: immediate mitigation closed. moving to monitoring/verification. setting follow-up alerts for prefix_miss_rate > 0.2 and scale_ops_rate_limit errors.

maria: handing off to next oncall @alex for verification and postmortem runbook. I'm going offline for urgent meetings.

alex: taking over. I'll keep monitoring for next 3h.

jake: filing customer followups and CC'ing product. severity set Sev2.

elena: quick notes for RCA: root cause appears to be a configuration regression in continuous-batching defaults combined with an aggressive prefix-cache TTL change. That led to cache missstorm, higher per-request latency -> fewer tokens/sec per GPU -> queue growth -> autoscaler hitting rate/quota caps and refusing scaledowns.

maria: agreed. next steps: 1) postmortem draft due EOD 2) add gate in deploy pipeline to block batch_window/prefix_ttl diffs > x% without perf review 3) add canary for prefix_cache_hit_rate and autoscaler scale ops rate as pre-deploy checks.

alex: noted. will create the postmortem skeleton and include metrics link + command snippets. cc: @sli-monitor for dashboard templating.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied, reduced customer impact. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring.

chris: thumbs up. closing pager.

maria: thanks team. good hustle.

alex: leaving final note: estimated customer impact window ~09:28 - 10:12 UTC, ~44 minutes. total affected customers: 4 (partial errors).

jake: assigning postmortem owners and timeline in INC-2981.

elena: adding follow-up action: limit future runtime config changes to canary pool first.

sli-monitor: NOTE: saved dashboard snapshots: https://grafana.redwood-infra/snapshot/queue-1766543210

alex: closing thread.
